ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Marshall Islands Domestic Sanctions Register (administered by the FIU). Each UBO, director, and senior officer must undergo name, passport number, and address screening. Enhanced due diligence applies for PEPs (foreign, domestic, or international organization) and equivalent senior officials. Screening frequency is at client on-boarding and on a rolling basis via automated sanctions tools. All screening records must be retained for 7 years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry (MICR) Online Name Reservation Portal – https://portal.registrar.gov.mh
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in English/Latin alphabetical characters (A–Z, 0–9). No diacritical marks, non-Latin scripts, or stylized symbols are permitted. The name must include a corporate suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Company', 'Incorporated', or 'Limited' (or the authorised abbreviation 'Corp.', 'Co.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.'). The name must be distinguishable from all existing names, and the registry applies an exact-character transliteration rule for names originally in a foreign script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include: (1) the proposed name, (2) reasons why the rejection is deemed erroneous, (3) supporting evidence of distinguishability, and (4) a non-refundable appeal fee of USD 150. The Registrar shall decide within 10 business days. If the name remains rejected, the applicant may submit a new reservation application. Once a reservation is granted, it is valid for 30 days and may be extended for an additional 30 days upon payment of USD 50.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-resident business corporation. A registered agent in the Marshall Islands must maintain a physical street address in Majuro (or Ebeye). Virtual office services for mail forwarding and director meeting facilities are acceptable for a crew recruitment agency, provided the registered agent's physical presence satisfies the statutory requirement. The company must retain all corporate books and records at the registered agent's address or at the principal place of business (which may be outside the Marshall Islands).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of incorporation, primarily driven by FIU compliance reviews and 2023 APG recommendations. The risk category is Low_Risk_Standard, but a maritime crew recruitment agency may trigger an onsite inspection if the registered agent is not sufficiently bonded or if the company holds a maritime crew agency license that requires verification of training certificates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (Title 27 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code), sections 10, 12, 22, and 32
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Majuro / Ebeye with online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed for issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; issued shares must be fully paid up at issuance; no escrow account requirement for a Non-Resident Business Corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the First Board Meeting of this Corporation is held by unanimous written consent; that the subscription for the Corporation's common stock by the initial shareholders is hereby accepted and issued at not less than par value; that the registered office be established at the address designated by the Marshall Islands Registered Agent and that such agent be retained; that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; that the President be and hereby is authorized to execute documents, open banking and payroll accounts, engage professional service providers, and take all necessary steps to obtain the statutory crew recruitment agency license; that all actions already taken by the incorporator and initial officers in furtherance of formation are ratified; this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the Registrar's online portal or through the licensed registered agent using the exact corporate name containing the required 'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'Limited', or approved abbreviation. Verify that the proposed name is distinguishable and not contrary to MIRC Title 27. Pay the name reservation fee online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because it is confusingly similar to an existing entity, file a revised reservation request with a written consent letter from the prior holder or select a new distinguishable corporate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation with Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (Corporate Registry Division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the executed Articles of Incorporation and the statutory fee package to the Registrar, either through the registered agent's submission portal or by direct filing with the Office of the Registrar. The Registrar will verify compliance with BCA formalities and issue an acknowledgment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice, correct the cited defect and resubmit within 30 days; pay the applicable deficiency fee; otherwise, reinstate by application under BCA section 34.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Statutory Fees and Receive Filing Receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Finance and Treasury Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the required incorporation fee, annual franchise tax deposit, and registered agent consent fee through wire transfer, bank draft, or the licensed registered agent's escrow account. Obtain official receipt evidencing payment.
required_dossiers: Proof of Wire Transfer or Certified Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Overpayment is refundable via written request; underpayment must be remedied by additional transfer within 14 days to avoid cancellation of the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review and fee clearance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation; the registered agent obtains the original certified copy. Confirm the certified corporate name, registered number, and date of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a certificate is delayed beyond SLA, contact the Registrar's support service with the filing receipt; if lost or defective, request certified replacement under official Registrar procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitute Initial Share Ledger and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registered Agent; Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the written consent or meeting of stakeholders approving share subscriptions; record the issuance of shares in the share register; adopt the Bylaws; file all formation documents in the corporate minute book maintained at the registered agent's office; issue share certificates to founding shareholders.
required_dossiers: Share Certificate Stubs and Transfer Ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any record is challenged by the Registrar or a financial institution, amend the record by dated corporate resolution and re-file with the registered agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator (MIMA), Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Maritime Affairs
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Agency License issued pursuant to Title 6 MIRC and MIMA Marine Notice No. 2-45-7

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Majuro
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Registration/Exempt (office-based crew agency; no manufacturing or marine terminal operations)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; office sewage connected to approved municipal sewer; no VOC-emitting operations; waste handling complies with solid waste disposal standards of the EPA and Majuro municipal regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate from the Majuro fire authority; structured load inspection letter for business occupancy; workplace standards clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Regulations of the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (portal: www.register-iri.com, administered by International Registries, Inc.); Customs and Revenue Division, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, RMI. The RMI maintains no income-tax filing authority for non-resident business corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN or VAT ID is issued by the RMI to non-resident Business Corporations (BCs) deriving exclusively foreign-source ship crew recruitment revenue. A foreign entity obtains: (1) a Certificate of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act from the Registrar of Corporations; (2) a Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade if any on-island presence exists; and (3) a Business Privilege Tax license only when physical business activity occurs on-island. The standard documentation package comprises a Certificate of Good Standing, a service-company affidavit, and the FIBL where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (Foreign Income Tax Act non-resident), taxed only on RMI-source income; ship crew recruitment and crew management services performed entirely offshore are outside the tax base.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under RMI law. The BC's tax status is governed by the non-resident declaration filed with the Registrar under the Business Corporations Act; an RMI LLC may alternatively file an election to be treated as a foreign disregarded investment vehicle, yielding no RMI entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax regime; the only indirect fiscal charges are RMI import customs duties on physical goods and the 3% Business Privilege Tax on gross receipts of on-island business activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST registration threshold exists in the RMI. The Business Privilege Tax imposes licensing from the first US Dollar (USD 0 threshold) of on-island gross receipts; pure offshore crew recruitment services do not trigger registration. Monetary amounts and records are USD-denominated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate exists. Physical import clearance runs through the Customs and Revenue Division's automated customs system (ASYCUDA) for goods only; crew recruitment service invoices remain standard commercial documents without government clearance or cryptographic stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — absent a VAT regime, there is no export VAT zero-rating claim. For vessels under the RMI flag, crew recruitment, payroll, and crew-management services supplied to non-resident shipowners are deemed performed wholly outside the Republic and are outside both the Foreign Income Tax Act and Business Privilege Tax bases; no refund mechanism exists to substantiate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (physical goods only; not applicable to crew recruitment services)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (physical shipments only)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank USD wire credit evidence retained for the RMI Maritime Administrator's crew-payroll verification)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RMI has no fraudulent zero-rating penalty because no zero-rating mechanism exists. Mischaracterizing on-island Business Privilege Tax-liable revenue as offshore triggers a 3% gross-receipts assessment, 12% annual interest, revocation of non-resident status, and a fine not exceeding USD 10,000 under the Business Privilege Tax Act; repeated false declarations expose the crew agency license to suspension by the RMI Maritime Administrator. The 180-day FX reference reflects the Maritime Administrator's maximum acceptable documentary gap between invoice date and inward remittance credit to the agency's USD account.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), acting in coordination with the U.S. Federal Reserve System and the U.S. Department of the Treasury. The RMI maintains no domestic central bank; the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender under the Compact of Free Association, and monetary policy is effectively set by the United States.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility for both capital and current account transactions because the RMI uses the U.S. dollar and imposes no foreign exchange controls. There are no statutory limits on inbound capital subscription or on outbound profit remittance. Non-resident Business Corporations have no RMI income tax liability and RMI law imposes no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees. The only practical hurdles are not statutory but regulatory and bank-driven, namely U.S. correspondent bank due diligence under the Bank Secrecy Act and OFAC compliance expectations, and the absence of a domestic interbank FX market, which forces all foreign currency conversion to be executed offshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The RMI maintains no exchange control regime, no export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory timeline for repatriation. Receipts from international crew recruitment and manning agency services may be retained indefinitely in USD or any freely convertible currency in any jurisdiction without any obligation to convert or surrender funds to a licensed bank. The only controlling obligations are the contractual terms of the underlying banking facility and standard FATF-aligned transaction monitoring, which does not impose surrender but does require transparent documentation of the source and purpose of funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Current Account (Standard) / Capital Escrow Account available for pre-license phase
Operational USD Corporate Account (primary clearing) / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability: LOW-to-MEDIUM. Legal constraints: (a) The RMI has no e-money or payment-institution licensing framework; deposit-taking is reserved to banks licensed under the RMI Banking Act, so foreign EMIs have no passporting rights into the RMI. (b) A non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation is generally treated as a higher-risk customer by offshore digital EMIs, and leading providers (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) typically decline RMI-incorporated entities or condition acceptance on substantive presence in a recognized jurisdiction such as the United States. (c) All USD settlement ultimately clears through the U.S. Federal Reserve network, exposing EMI providers to U.S. correspondent and sanctions compliance risk. (d) The RMI offers no deposit insurance. Recommended work-around: maintain the primary operating and treasury account at a licensed RMI bank with a U.S. correspondent chain, and use offshore EMIs only as secondary disbursement tools, with each EMI position fully mirrored by an RMI bank master account and subject to daily reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is generally required for at least one director and every authorized signatory, either at the Majuro branch of the chosen bank or before a notary public in the director's jurisdiction using notarized specimen signatures. Remote video-KYC is not accepted as a substitute where the RMI bank relies on U.S. correspondent due diligence. The bank will require apostilled or notarized corporate documents, including the Business Corporation charter, board resolutions opening accounts and designating signatories, a current certificate of good standing, the UBO declaration, and proof of a physical registered office in RMI. In-country appearance may be waived for non-executive directors if the local registered agent certifies identity against a passport and the bank approves the waiver; however, at least one physically present or locally represented director is strongly advisable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident domestic corporation with no RMI tax liability and no physical office being classified as a shell or letterbox entity under FATF and correspondent banking standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of good standing; certified copy of the Business Corporation Act charter and by-laws; confirmation of registration on the RMI Registrar's Beneficial Ownership Register; full shareholder register with no bearer shares; UBO identification documents with apostille; board resolution approving account opening and designated signatories; certified copy of the statutory ship crew recruitment and manning agency license issued by the RMI Maritime Administrator; a substance narrative evidencing registered office, registered agent, periodic board meetings, and a treasury services agreement with an administration provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity maritime remittance flows to seafarers in multiple high-risk jurisdictions (Philippines, Indonesia, India, Bangladesh), triggering money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions screening concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved crew payroll ledger with STCW certificate of competency or flag state seafarer document numbers; executed employment or collective bargaining agreements; copies of seafarer passports and CDC/seaman's books; group AML/CFT policy with transaction monitoring thresholds and suspicious transaction reporting procedures; pre-payroll sanctions screening of every beneficiary seafarer and vessel owner against OFAC, UN, EU, and UK consolidated lists; written confirmation that no vessel managed by the agency is engaged in sanctioned trades.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of source of funds and source of wealth for inbound capital subscription from foreign shareholders, particularly where a shareholder is a politically exposed person or located in a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements and documentary chain evidencing the provenance of shareholder funds, such as salary vouchers, sale and purchase agreements, audited financial statements, or realized investment proceeds; passport and notarized or apostilled identification for each UBO; complete corporate ownership chain diagram from the entity through to natural persons; PEP screening report and, if applicable, an enhanced due diligence assessment approved by the bank's compliance committee; certified consent from any regulatory authority contributing to the shareholder's funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputation and jurisdiction risk triggered by third-country listings or mutual evaluation follow-up measures affecting the Marshall Islands, causing automatic escalation at U.S. correspondent banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written tax compliance summary confirming RMI non-resident corporation exemption from income tax and absence of any tax-planning purpose; evidence of genuine economic substance, including local registered agent, physical registered office, and operational contracts; Wolfsberg-style correspondent bank transparency questionnaire completed by the RMI bank; annual AML/CFT certification and independent audit report of the agency's compliance program; evidence that the agency supports legitimate vessel owners and no link to illegal, unreported, or unregulated fishing or sanctions evasive shipping.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant USD routing is executed exclusively by SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) or MT202 with cover through a U.S. correspondent bank because the RMI has no RTGS system. A recommended chain uses Bank of Guam (ABA 121405105) or Bank of Hawaii as the receiving correspondent, crediting the MH_BC account at the licensed RMI bank. The remitter name on the SWIFT message must match the shareholder KYC record on file, and field 70 remittance information must state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - NON-RESIDENT BUSINESS CORPORATION' or similar. The receiving bank will require, before release of funds, a board resolution approving the capital injection, UBO source-of-funds documentation, and evidence of the statutory crew recruitment license. No RMI capital duty, stamp duty, or registration tax applies, and no statutory purpose-code regime exists, so the remittance narrative must follow the receiving bank's own compliance template.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for crew payroll runs, principal shipowner settlements, and vendor payments. MT202 or MT202 COV is used only for funding intermediate accounts and interbank positions between the RMI bank and its U.S. or Asian correspondents. Commercial letters of credit may be opened for large manning service contracts where the shipowner requires documentary proof of shipment of crewing services, but routine payroll dispersal is executed through MT103 push payments to beneficiary banks. For multi-currency crew payroll, funds are swept from the USD treasury account to a licensed payout aggregator or the crew member's local bank using local real-time rails: PESONet in the Philippines, BI-FAST in Indonesia, IMPS/RTP in India, SEPA in eurozone jurisdictions, and FedACH/CHIPS in the United States. Every outbound MT103 must carry structured ISO 20022 remittance information including crew name, payroll contract reference, and period, and must pass OFAC, UN, EU, and UK sanctions screening before release. U.S.-dollar liquidity can be optimized through a Fedwire-funded master concentration account at the correspondent bank with automated zero-balancing sweeps.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward contracts (USD versus EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD) executed with U.S.-licensed or Hong Kong licensed banks under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with CSA collateral terms

Non-deliverable FX forward contracts (NDFs) for non-deliverable crew remittance currencies (Philippine peso, Indian rupee, Indonesian rupiah, Bangladeshi taka) settled in USD against WM/Refinitiv or HKMA CLS fixing rates
Cross-currency swaps (FXS/CCS) matching the agency's multi-currency payroll payable portfolio with USD receivables from shipowners, including tenor-matched interest and principal exchanges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration Statement and Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation, no later than the last day of the incorporation anniversary month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty accrues at 10% per month; continued default for more than 180 days triggers administrative dissolution and loss of legal capacity to operate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent and Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Registration Statement; updates required within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or change in control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current beneficial ownership data may result in administrative penalties, rejection of subsequent corporate filings, and referral to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit for non-compliance with anti-money-laundering obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Maritime Crew Recruitment and Placement Service License
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RMI Maritime Administrator, Republic of the Marshall Islands Ship Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually prior to the expiration of the current license period; calendar-year licensees must file by December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or non-renewal of crew recruitment license; prohibition on further seafarer placement activity; removal from the approved list of recruitment and placement services under STCW and MLC, 2006

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based compulsory audit is imposed on a non-resident private Business Corporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act. A certified independent audit is mandatory when: (i) the company is listed or publicly traded; (ii) shareholders holding at least 20% of the voting power make a written audit demand; (iii) the articles, bylaws, or a shareholders agreement expressly require an audit; or (iv) the RMI Maritime Administrator requires audited financial statements as a condition for renewal of the crew recruitment license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, or US GAAP, applied consistently; books and records must be maintained in English and in a manner that accurately presents the financial condition of the corporation and enables financial statements to be prepared

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each non-resident Business Corporation must maintain a current beneficial ownership register at its registered agent's office and file an annual beneficial ownership confirmation with the Annual Registration Statement. The confirmation must identify every individual or entity that directly or indirectly owns 10% or more of the shares, controls voting power, or exercises ultimate control; any transfer of shares resulting in a change of such ownership must be reported to the registered agent and reflected in the annual confirmation within 30 days of the transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 - US$10,000 per engagement if a certified audit becomes required; voluntary review or compilation of financial statements typically US$1,500 - US$4,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — the Marshall Islands (RMI) levies no corporate income tax; a non-resident domestic Business Corporation is statutorily exempt from all taxes on income under Section 213 of the RMI Business Corporations Act.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No profit-based tax holiday or deduction regime exists. The only mandatory annual impost is a de minimis registration/franchise fee payable to the Registrar of Corporations; a crew recruitment agency additionally bears Maritime Administrator licensing and vessel manning fees, none of which are profit-based.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Business Corporation Annual Report (Form BC-AR) filed with the RMI Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, via the Registrar's official e-filing portal or authorized registered agent. No corporate income tax return exists in the RMI.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filing and fee payment are due on or before the corporation's anniversary of incorporation; a short statutory grace period applies, after which late-payment charges accrue and strike-off proceedings may commence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name and registration number as stated on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered name; do not indicate any RMI trade, business, or payroll activity in the descriptive fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and statutory registered agent located in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed RMI registered agent must be named; this address is a legal-representation address only and does not, by itself, create RMI taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address and head-office jurisdiction of the crew recruitment and manning agency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the overseas principal office (e.g., Manila, Singapore, Limassol); do not overstate RMI premises where no operational substance exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and corporate officers with full names, residential addresses, and nationality.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: RMI law permits all non-resident directors; disclose each director's physical residential address. Any nominee arrangement must be separately disclosed to the registered agent for AML purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, par value, and shareholder class details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital applies; declare accurate issued capital. Under-capitalization combined with large multi-currency payroll flows is a classic veil-piercing trigger for foreign courts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership and AML/CFT customer due diligence declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Registrar maintains beneficial-ownership information; confirm ultimate natural persons and state that passport/KYC and source-of-funds records for crew payments are held on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of exempt non-resident status and absence of RMI-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that no RMI-source commercial activity occurred during the year; no profit and loss statement, no balance sheet, and no tax computation is submitted because the RMI has no operating income tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late fee payment trigger statutory surcharges on the annual registration fee; continuing default leads to administrative strike-off from the RMI register, loss of corporate capacity, and nullification of manning agreements. Officers trading after strike-off are personally exposed to civil and regulatory action, and reinstatement requires arrears, penalties, and court-ordered restoration costs.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the RMI imposes no dividend withholding tax; distributions declared by a non-resident Business Corporation to shareholders are entirely outside the RMI withholding framework.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive double tax avoidance agreement covering dividends. Relief is evidenced by obtaining an RMI Certificate of Good Standing / Non-Assessment from the Registrar of Corporations, confirming zero RMI tax liability, for presentation to the shareholder's home revenue authority. For shipping-adjacent income, the BC may invoke flag-reciprocity exemption (e.g., U.S. IRC Section 883) with a certificate of corporate existence and vessel documentation; no RMI treaty reduction route exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory and no treaty override: no RMI withholding tax applies to outbound royalties for crew-management software or vessel-operations IP, nor to interest on intercompany financing extended by the BC. Conversely, no RMI withholding is applied to payments made by the BC to foreign licensors or lenders, given the absence of a domestic withholding statute.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None — the RMI has no enacted transfer-pricing statute, no Local File/Master File filing obligation, and no statutory threshold in local currency (the functional currency is the U.S. dollar). Nevertheless, the BC must contemporaneously document intercompany commission rates, payroll-funding arrangements, and margin benchmarks, because the crew-buyer's home jurisdiction will apply its own arm's-length rules to the agency fee.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI applies an OECD/EU-aligned Economic Substance framework. A non-resident BC carrying on any RMI relevant activity, including crew supply or vessel management connected to RMI-flagged tonnage, must demonstrate locally directed and managed operations, adequate employees and premises, proportionate expenditure, and must file an annual economic substance return. A pure offshore recruitment and payroll agency operating from a foreign head office, with no RMI management or core income-generating activity, is exempt from the charging net but must retain payroll contracts, KYC records, and substance evidence to withstand foreign tax authority review.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Facilitation of Foreign Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC as a conduit to conceal crew-agency revenue from foreign tax authorities, issuing fictitious seafarer employment contracts or inflated payroll invoices to reduce employer social-security and income taxes in crew-supply jurisdictions, or backdating crew disbursements to manipulate taxable periods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under the RMI Criminal Code for money laundering and fraudulent dealing: fines up to USD 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 25 years, plus civil forfeiture of wire-transfer proceeds and commission income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating or maintaining a 'non-resident' BC with no office, no director meetings, no payroll operations, and no employees, used solely to hold crewmanning contracts while actual recruitment, invoicing, and decision-making occur in another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off and deregistration by the Registrar for annual-report default; court-ordered restoration with penalties; economic-substance penalties for failure to file the annual substance return; foreign tax authorities may disregard the BC as a sham and reallocate the agency profit to the real operating entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach in Payroll and Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Swift Wire and multi-currency seafarer payroll rails without customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership transparency, or source-of-funds verification; processing third-party payroll wires on forged seafarer identity documents; failing to file suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and regulatory sanctions under the RMI AML/CFT framework, suspension or revocation of the crew recruitment license and RMI vessel manning approvals, per-day fines for beneficial-ownership record failures, and naming by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Placing seafarers on RMI-flagged vessels or supplying crews under RMI manning approvals without the statutory crew-agency license issued by the RMI Maritime Administrator, or engaging unlicensed sub-agents in foreign manning hubs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Statutory fines and imprisonment under RMI maritime and seafarer protection legislation; the Maritime Administrator may detain the vessel, order crew disembarkation, void the manning agreement, and register unpaid seafarer wages as a maritime lien against the vessel.

stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors_consolid: Directors and beneficial owners face statutory veil-piercing under the RMI Business Corporations Act where the corporation is a mere instrumentality of fraud. Consequences include personal civil restitution to foreign tax authorities and defrauded seafarers, asset forfeiture, travel bans imposed by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit or Maritime Administrator pending resolution of crew wage claims, disqualification from RMI-flagged vessel registration, extradition exposure in egregious wage-theft and money-laundering cases, and imprisonment.
